data.name: Randy Lander
data.bio: A Caracas native who led global campaigns at The Boeing Company for 20 years before founding the Foundation.
data.long_bio:
Randy Lander is the Founder and Chairman of Victoria Venezuela Foundation (VVF), a faith-based nonprofit committed to transforming the lives of vulnerable children and families throughout Venezuela. Guided by his faith in Jesus Christ and a deep commitment to servant leadership, Randy leads a network of more than 100 volunteers delivering education, nutrition, healthcare, and family-support programs to more than 700 children.

A native of Caracas, Venezuela, Randy founded VVF from a personal desire to serve his home country and create lasting opportunities for its most vulnerable communities. Under his leadership, the Foundation has expanded its programs, strengthened its local partnerships, and established a sustainable model of care centered on dignity, hope, and the love of Christ.

Randy is also the Founder and President of Luminis Global Partners, a U.S.-based global holding company with operations across Latin America, including Venezuela. Previously, he built a distinguished 20-year career at The Boeing Company, where he held senior leadership roles across the Americas, Europe, Asia, and the Middle East. During his tenure, he led multinational teams, managed global portfolios, and directed more than $30 billion in commercial aircraft and services campaigns. His international experience included assignments in Japan and South Korea and advisory work with airline boards, government stakeholders, customers, and strategic partners.

Throughout his career, Randy has remained deeply committed to community service. He has held leadership and board positions supporting children, education, and community-development initiatives, including Special Olympics Washington, the Society of Manufacturing Engineers, and the Boeing Employees Community Fund in Japan.

Randy holds degrees in Mechanical and Manufacturing Engineering and a Master of Business Administration. He and his wife, Helen, have two children and share a passion for faith, service, travel, and creating a lasting legacy of hope for the people of Venezuela.
data.quote: Randy is passionate about serving God and about servant leadership.

data.name: Helen Bello
data.bio: Field Marketing Manager at Microsoft, formerly eight years at The Boeing Company. MBA, University of Washington.
data.long_bio:
Helen Bello is Co-Founder of The Victoria Venezuela Foundation. A Venezuelan native, Helen has resided in the United States for 28 years and has never lost contact with her Venezuelan roots. She has served on multiple boards of directors throughout the years, including the Association of Latino Professionals For America (ALPFA) and Seattle Credit Union. She currently works at Microsoft as a Field Marketing Manager, where she is responsible for building customer insight-driven marketing strategies and campaigns for a set of strategic accounts. Before Microsoft, she spent eight years at The Boeing Company.

She served in a variety of customer relationship, procurement, and marketing roles. Helen has experience with large accounts, providing marketing engagement with customer account executives across North and Latin America. She led cross-functional teams focused on business development, strategy integration, sales and marketing analytics, and post-sales technology integration. Helen holds both a bachelor’s degree and a Master of Business Administration from the University of Washington.

data.name: Charmiant Corado
data.bio: Emmy Award-winning communications professional with more than ten years in media and digital content, formerly with WarnerMedia and Gray Media.
data.long_bio:
Charmiant Corado is an Emmy Award-winning communications professional with more than 10 years of experience in media, digital communications, and content strategy. She currently serves as Director of Communications & Digital Platforms for the Victoria Venezuela Foundation, where she leads digital communications, storytelling, social media, and outreach initiatives that help amplify the Foundation’s mission and impact.

Throughout her career, Charmiant has worked in fast-paced media and communications environments, including WarnerMedia and Gray Media, developing content and communications strategies for diverse audiences. She holds master's degrees in Communication Management from Emerson College and Mass Media Communication from Complutense University of Madrid.

Passionate about using communications to create meaningful connections and amplify positive change, Charmiant is proud to support the Foundation’s work helping children, families, and communities in Venezuela.

data.name: Juan Tomasini
data.long_bio:
Juan is a South Florida–based contractor, entrepreneur, and Co-Founder of The Trusty Handyman, a family-owned company providing reliable, high-quality improvement services to homeowners and businesses throughout the region.

Drawing on a third-generation construction background, Juan has dedicated his career to the home services and construction industry. Juan is passionate about building meaningful relationships, creating opportunities, and pursuing continuous personal and professional growth. Outside of work, he enjoys playing golf, exercising, reading, and spending quality time with his family.

data.name: Enrique Flores
data.bio: Founder and CEO of Paula Inc. Responsible for the Foundation’s branding and digital presence.
data.long_bio:
Enrique is the Executive Vice President, Digital Transformation at Victoria Venezuela Foundation. He also supports its fundraising.

He is the founder and CEO of Paula Inc., a Toronto agency that builds brands, websites, and marketing systems for financial services companies. Before starting Paula, he spent more than ten years inside the wealth management industry in Toronto, rising to Chief Marketing Officer.

At the foundation, Enrique is responsible for branding and digital presence. His job is to make sure the depth, legitimacy, vision and achievements of the organization come through in everything people see of it online.

He was born in Caracas and lives in Toronto. Outside work he follows politics, keeps up his fitness, and snowboards when the season allows. He believes in a world that works for everyone.
data.quote: I believe in a world that works for everyone.

data.name: Dorceia Watkins
data.long_bio:
Dorceia J. McCullough-Watkins, PhD is a development strategist, grant professional, writer, educator, and entrepreneur committed to helping those who help others. As the Founder and Principal Consultant of Inspirational Editions (IE), she helps nonprofits, faith-based organizations, and small businesses strengthen their capacity, communicate their vision, secure funding, and achieve measurable organizational impact.

With close to a decade of experience in grant development, proposal writing, contracts, organizational development, and strategic communications, Dorceia has supported organizations pursuing millions of dollars in public and private funding. Her experience spans nonprofit services, workforce development, transportation, social services, faith-based initiatives, community development, and small-business growth. She brings a unique combination of writing expertise, organizational leadership, grant strategy, and program-development knowledge to every engagement.

Dr. McCullough-Watkins holds a PhD in Christian Education and an MBA in Organizational Leadership, along with a bachelor’s degree in Biblical Studies and Worship Ministry. She continuously strives to reflect her belief that effective leadership requires both strategic excellence and a commitment to purpose.

Through Inspirational Editions, Dorceia equips leaders to transform ideas into sustainable initiatives, strengthen organizations from the inside out, and pursue opportunities that create meaningful community impact. Her guiding philosophy is simple: help those who help others.

data.name: Arivana Rangel
data.bio: More than a decade leading social-impact programs and public-private partnerships; psychologist with a Master in Public Administration from IESA.
data.long_bio:
Arivana brings more than a decade of experience in strategic social impact planning, multidisciplinary project management, and community engagement. She has led multisectoral programs for non-profit organizations and foundations, strengthening public-private partnerships and advancing high-impact social initiatives.

Her background includes conducting needs assessments, designing and overseeing programs, and facilitating multi-stakeholder collaboration to improve outcomes and ensure long-term sustainability. Arivana’s work reflects a commitment to building structures that expand opportunity, empower communities, and generate measurable, lasting impact.

Arivana Rangel Durán holds a Bachelor’s degree in Psychology from Universidad Católica Andrés Bello (Caracas, Venezuela), a Master in Public Administration from the Instituto de Estudios Superiores de Administración (IESA), and is certified by the Entrepreneurship Program at Babson College (Boston, Massachusetts, USA).

data.name: Johnny Yataco
data.bio: Publisher of Washington Hispanic, which he founded in 1994; named Businessman of the Year by the Peruvian American Chamber of Commerce in 2008.
data.long_bio:
Johnny A. Yataco, publisher of Washington Hispanic, was born and raised in Lima, Peru. From an early age, he was exposed to the publishing world. His mother often took him to work with her at a daily newspaper in Lima. He has always had a natural entrepreneurial spirit.

At age 18, he attended Foto Interamericana del Perú, an institute of the Eastman Kodak Company, to study photography. He later went on to study artificial intelligence at Oxford University.

He worked for several newspapers in Peru and then spent two years in the Office of Communications for the President of Peru at the time.

In February 1994, he began his own publication, Washington Hispanic. Today it has 28 full-time employees and more than 30 freelance support personnel. It has been recognized by the National Association of Hispanic Publications (NAHP), and in 1999 it ranked No. 54 among the fastest-growing Hispanic companies in the United States. Johnny has received awards from community organizations including the Ibero American Chamber of Commerce, which named his organization Small Business of the Year in 1998, and the Peruvian American Chamber of Commerce, which named him Businessman of the Year in 2008.

data.name: Luis Arias
data.bio: Venezuelan audiovisual producer who leads the executive production of two national television programs and serves a network of more than 35,000 churches.
data.long_bio:
Luis Arias is a Venezuelan social communicator and audiovisual producer with extensive experience in operational direction, field production, and the coordination of national and international satellite broadcasts. He holds a degree in Social Communication with a concentration in Audiovisual Media from Universidad Santa María, as well as advanced master’s-level training in Executive Production for Film and Television.

Luis began his media career through hands-on experience in radio and broadcast television. Motivated by the industry’s rigorous technical and operational standards, he pursued formal academic training and later joined major international networks. His professional experience includes managing technical production and logistics for ESPN Latin America’s continental baseball broadcasts, as well as supporting operational deployment and executive production for multimedia content at FOX.

In Venezuela, Luis has continued to develop his expertise in live television and currently leads the executive production of two nationally broadcast programs: Despertar on Televisora Venezolana Social (TVes) and La Jornada on Venezolana de Televisión (VTV).

A profound personal and spiritual transformation a decade ago redirected Luis’s professional calling toward communications with a ministerial purpose. Since then, he has used his technical expertise, media relationships, and production experience to develop platforms that expand the reach of the Gospel through regional, national, and international television.

Following the pandemic, his ministry-focused communications work has grown significantly. Luis now serves as a communications liaison and representative for a network of more than 35,000 churches, coordinating opportunities for pastors and spiritual leaders to share their messages through national and regional media. He also develops strategic partnerships with leading Venezuelan media organizations and provides technical and communications support to international ministries, helping bring the Gospel into influential institutional and media spaces.

His life and work are guided by a simple conviction: “Apart from Him, we can do nothing.”

data.name: Ximena Sosa
data.bio: Bilingual digital marketing lead with more than eight years at mission-driven organizations, including Compassion International and Save the Children.
data.long_bio:
Ximena Sosa is a bilingual digital marketing and communications professional with more than eight years of experience supporting nonprofit, humanitarian, and mission-driven organizations. She currently serves as Senior Director of Digital Strategy at Victoria Venezuela Foundation, where she leads digital marketing and communications initiatives designed to strengthen awareness, donor engagement, fundraising, and community connection.

In her role, Ximena oversees integrated digital strategies across web, email, social media, paid media, SEO, analytics, and digital campaigns. She also helps shape bilingual messaging and storytelling for donors, volunteers, partners, and the broader community, ensuring that communications remain consistent with the Foundation’s mission and amplify the impact of its work serving Venezuelan communities.

Prior to joining Victoria Venezuela Foundation, Ximena held digital marketing and communications roles with Compassion International, Save the Children, and Catholic Relief Services, where she contributed to fundraising, advocacy, donor acquisition, audience engagement, and Hispanic marketing initiatives.

Ximena holds a Bachelor of Arts in Marketing and International Business from Florida International University and is fluent in English and Spanish. Her work reflects a commitment to using strategic communications to connect people with meaningful opportunities to serve, give, and create lasting impact.

data.name: Elimar Ugueto
data.bio: Founder and CEO of Ugueto AI with 25 years in media and marketing; leads the design of the Foundation's agentic systems.
data.long_bio:
Elimar Ugueto is the Founder and CEO of Ugueto AI, with more than 25 years of experience spanning media, corporate communications, and marketing. Her career began in television in Venezuela and later expanded to U.S. Hispanic media, including Univision and ESPN Deportes, as well as project work for global brands such as Amazon, Google, Johnson & Johnson, Oreo, FIFA and Coca-Cola, among others.

Elimar joined Victoria Venezuela Foundation as a Marketing Advisor, initially supporting the organization’s marketing and production efforts. As her professional focus evolved from traditional digital marketing toward the practical implementation of AI and agentic systems, her role at VVF evolved as well. Today, she leads the design and development of the Foundation’s agentic systems, working directly with team members and subject-matter experts to understand their workflows. She translates operational needs into practical AI-powered solutions across marketing, research, events, fundraising, and internal operations.

Born in Venezuela and bilingual in English and Spanish, Elimar brings a personal connection to VVF’s mission. She holds a certification in CS50: Computer Science for Business from Harvard University. Guided by her Christian faith, she believes technology is a form of stewardship — and every system she builds has one purpose: freeing the team’s time and attention so it can go where it matters most, serving the children God has entrusted to this Foundation.

data.name: Vanessa Sanchez
data.bio: Communications professional with six years at the University of South Florida and the University of Tampa; master's degree in Cybersecurity.
data.long_bio:
Vanessa has over six years of combined experience working at the University of South Florida and the University of Tampa, specializing in communication and academic customer service. She holds a bachelor’s degree in Mass Communication from the University of South Florida and a master’s degree in Cybersecurity from the University of Tampa. Vanessa’s unique combination of skills enables her to manage social media communications while helping ensure the integrity and security of sensitive data in today’s evolving IT landscape.

Originally from Caracas, Venezuela, Vanessa brings a multicultural perspective to her work, enriching her approach to communication and collaboration. She is deeply passionate about supporting communities in need, and her empathetic approach to problem-solving, combined with her dedication to fostering positive change, makes her a valuable asset in nonprofit environments.

In addition to her professional work, Vanessa is an entrepreneur who runs a personal blog called Meet Me in Tampa, where she highlights the city’s food scene and natural beauty. Her blog reflects her love for her community and her enthusiasm for showcasing the positive aspects of the city.

data.name: Antonio Manzanares
data.long_bio:
Full-stack software engineer who brings his technical skills to VVF's website and online presence.

Antonio Manzanares serves as Senior Developer for the Victoria Venezuela Foundation, supporting the organization's website and digital presence so that VVF's mission reaches the people who need to see it.

Antonio is a full-stack software engineer at DealMaker, a fintech platform for online capital raises, where his work spans everything from issuer onboarding features to production incident response. Before moving into engineering, he spent nearly a decade in B2B sales, a background that shapes how he approaches problem-solving and working with people today.

Outside of his day job, Antonio also runs anclist web dev, building sites and digital tools for clients and organizations he believes in.

Originally from Caracas, Venezuela, and now based in Toronto, Antonio is fluent in Spanish and stays closely connected to his roots. He and his wife are raising their child together, and he believes our purpose is to serve with the talents we've been given — volunteering his skills with VVF is one way he lives that out.
data.quote: "Our purpose is to serve with the talents we've been given."

data.name: David Cardenas
data.bio: Pastor of Ebenezer Church of Christ in Ciudad Bolívar with more than two decades in pastoral ministry and community service.
data.long_bio:
Pastor David Cárdenas is a devoted Christian leader with more than two decades of experience in pastoral ministry, biblical teaching, and community service. Born and raised in a Christian home, he developed a strong foundation of faith and family values from an early age and answered God’s call to ministry while still young.

As Pastor of Ebenezer Church of Christ, David combines youthful energy with deep ministerial experience, allowing him to connect meaningfully with both emerging generations and longtime members of the Church. His leadership is characterized by compassion, spiritual maturity, and a commitment to helping individuals and families grow in their relationship with Jesus Christ.

Together with his wife and their two daughters, Pastor David has faithfully embraced a family-centered calling to serve God and the community. They have been instrumental in developing the Church’s children’s ministry and preparing young leaders to serve the next generation with excellence and purpose.

His passion for children, families, and community transformation strongly reflects the mission of Victoria Venezuela Foundation: sharing God’s love while creating lasting hope and opportunities for those most in need.

data.title: Fiscal 2025 transparency report
data.author: Victoria Venezuela Foundation
data.excerpt: 95% of funds went directly to programs in fiscal 2025.

data.question: How much does sponsorship cost?
data.answer: Sponsorship starts at $25 per month. You choose the amount that fits your budget. Your gifts fund the meals, medical care and education programs that reach every child in our care. In fiscal 2025, 95% of funds went directly to programs.

data.question: Where does my money go?
data.answer: Your sponsorship funds provide weekly meals, medical checkups twice a year, school supplies and uniforms, and faith-based teaching. We maintain complete transparency about how every dollar is spent. You can review our detailed financials anytime on our website.

data.question: Can I write to my sponsored child?
data.answer: Yes. Your child will receive your letters and drawings, and they will write back to you. This connection is one of the most meaningful parts of sponsorship.

data.question: What updates will I receive?
data.answer: You'll receive letters and photos from your child, along with annual impact reports showing how your sponsorship changed their life. We also send prayer requests and updates about their progress in school and health.

data.question: Can I send gifts to my child?
data.answer: We recommend keeping gifts modest and practical, such as school supplies or books. Large or expensive gifts can create complications. We'll guide you on what works best for your child's situation and community.

data.question: Does my money go directly to my sponsored child?
data.answer: Your sponsorship connects you with one child. Gifts are combined to fund the nutrition, medical care and education that reach every child in our programs, which keeps support steady for each child even if a sponsor steps away.

data.question: Are donations tax-deductible?
data.answer: Yes. Victoria Venezuela Foundation is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization. All donations are tax-deductible to the fullest extent allowed by law. You'll receive a receipt for your records.

data.question: How is my money used?
data.answer: Ninety-five percent of funds go directly to programs. We support nutrition, medical care, and education for children in Venezuela. See our financials page for a complete breakdown.

data.question: Can I designate my gift?
data.answer: Absolutely. You can direct your gift to a specific program or child sponsorship. Let us know your preference when you give, or contact us to discuss options.

data.question: How do I get a receipt?
data.answer: A receipt is sent automatically after your donation. Check your email, including spam folders. For recurring gifts, you'll receive an annual summary.

data.question: Can I cancel recurring gifts?
data.answer: Yes. You can change or cancel your monthly gift anytime. No questions asked. Contact us or manage your subscription through your donor account.

data.question: What is the format of the tournament?
data.answer: We play a Scramble format to keep the pace fun and inclusive for all skill levels. Team up and bring your best!

data.question: Where is the event being held?
data.answer: The Club at Weston Hills, Weston, Florida, located at 2600 Country Club Way, Weston, FL 33332. Complimentary parking is available onsite, and signage will guide you to registration.

data.question: Are donations tax-deductible?
data.answer: Yes. Victoria Venezuela Foundation is a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization. Tax ID: 88-3282100. Contributions are tax-deductible under Internal Revenue Code Section 501(c)(3).

data.question: Can I donate an item or service for the raffle or auction?
data.answer: Yes, and we deeply appreciate your support! Donating an item or service is a powerful way to contribute to our mission while showcasing your brand or talents to a passionate and engaged audience. We welcome a wide range of contributions, including:Gift baskets (gourmet foods, spa items, themed collections)Experiences (golf outings, weekend getaways, dining packages)Professional services (photography sessions, wellness consultations, coaching)Unique items (artwork, memorabilia, handcrafted goods)To donate, email us at charitygolf@victoriavenezuelafoundation.org with a brief description of the item or service, its estimated fair market value, and your contact information and business name (if applicable).

Executive summary

Welcome to the Victoria Venezuela Foundation! We are a non-profit organization 501(c)(3), dedicated to embed the love of Jesus to our most vulnerable children in Venezuela, bringing to each community critical food and medical attention.
Since our inception in July 2022, we firmly placed our hearts to God and commenced planting our initial seeds with a clear mission -
design a local support network investing in the well being of these children and the future of Venezuela.
We have been humbled and appreciative of the overwhelming support by the community, volunteers and companies propelling the faith and establishing strong core and long-term values for these children.
Our passionate and relentless team established two local support centers in:
Los Valles del Tuy, Miranda and Ciudad Bolivar, Bolivar
supporting both food and medical attention programs. Below is a brief snapshot of the work that was accomplished in 2022:
nutritional plates served to at risk children
children received critical medical attention
companies investing and sponsoring support programs

We can’t wait to see the new thousand smiles and filled hearts this new year with your continued support. We look forward to 2023 with an even stronger determination and abundant faith on what God continues to do in Venezuela.
Randy & Helen

Partners

Centro Cristiano Luz de Las Naciones (CCLN) is a Ministry founded over 30 years ago in Los Valles Del Tuy, Miranda Venezuela. MVV together with Pastor Jose Guerrero, launched 12 different nutrition centers across the city supporting over 400 children every week.

Frequently asked questions
What did Victoria Venezuela Foundation achieve in 2022?
More than 5,000 nutritional plates were served to at-risk children, 52 children received critical medical attention, and 5 companies invested in and sponsored the support programs.
How much went to charitable programs in 2022?

Does the foundation spend money on administration?

A message from us

As we reflect on our journey in 2023, it has been incredible to witness first hand how our community continues to come together in support of children and Venezuela. We commenced our year with an unwavering commitment to our mission:
Design support networks throughout Venezuela with nutrition and medical attention programs while teaching children to have a personal relationship with Jesus Christ.

Our volunteers and partners continued to grow with a vivid calling to serve and make a difference. We wanted to extend our heartfelt appreciation for your partnership and generous support. We delivered and exceeded expectations across the support programs bringing joy and hope to children’s lives.
Below is a brief snapshot of the work that together we accomplished in 2023:
nutritional plates served to at risk children
Babies and children received critical medical attention
corporations sponsoring support programs and investing in Venezuela

At each of the support centers across, we could see each week how children’s lives were being transformed. Their palpable desire to attend at first in desperate need of help. Little by little, we could see a light being ignited as they commence their journey to learn more about their heavenly Father, God.

As the team commences this new year, with great anticipation, we look forward to continue being part of the transformative work that God is doing in Venezuela. We hope you are as well. We have big plans and dreams for these children’s future, and we invite you to join us in this journey of faith and love.
With blessings,
Randy & Helen

data.title: How to sponsor a child directly, without going through a large charity

authors.name: Randy Lander
authors.role: Founder and Chairman, Victoria Venezuela Foundation

data.excerpt: Direct child sponsorship means your monthly gift supports an identified child through a specific organization, and you can see where the money goes.

children.text: The short answer

Direct child sponsorship means your monthly gift supports an identified child through a specific organization, and you can see where the money goes. Large US programs ask $39 to $43 a month. The main trade-off against a large international charity is scale versus proximity: big organizations have more infrastructure, smaller ones can tell you the name of the person who handed a child their meal.

At Victoria Venezuela Foundation, sponsorship starts at $25 a month. Your sponsorship connects you with one child, and gifts fund the nutrition, medical care and education programs that reach every child in our care. In fiscal 2025, 95% of funds went directly to programs.
What “sponsoring a child” actually means

Child sponsorship is a recurring monthly donation connected to a specific child. In most programs the sponsor receives updates, and often letters or photographs, so the relationship is visible rather than abstract.

What it does not mean, and this is the most common misunderstanding: your money does not go to that child as cash. It funds the programs that child is enrolled in. A $25 monthly gift does not become $25 in a family’s hands. It becomes a share of a meal program, a clinic visit, a set of school supplies.

That distinction matters because it is also what makes sponsorship work. Programs serve groups. A child benefits because the program around them exists, and pooled gifts keep support steady for every child even when a sponsor steps away.
Why people look for a direct option
Three reasons come up repeatedly.

They want to know where the money goes. Large charities publish audited financials, which is genuinely more than most small ones do. But the answer arrives as a percentage in an annual report, not as a photograph of the classroom.
They want a real connection.
Sponsors who have given for years often say they never heard from the child in a way that felt personal.
They want their money concentrated.
A smaller organization working in one country puts more of each dollar into a place the donor chose deliberately.
None of those are arguments that large charities are bad. They are large because they are effective at scale, and scale saves lives. They are arguments about what a particular donor is looking for.
Direct sponsorship compared with a large international charity

content.text: Rare, and usually a formal trip

children.text: Large-charity costs are the published monthly rates of World Vision, Plan International USA, Children International and Compassion International, as of September 2026. Check each organization’s current rate.
How to sponsor a child directly, step by step
Pick a country or a cause, not an organization. Start with where you want the money to go. The list of organizations narrows quickly once you do.
Verify the organization is a registered charity.
In the United States that means a 501(c)(3) designation and an EIN. You can check any EIN for free on the
IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search
ProPublica’s Nonprofit Explorer
, or
Candid
Read the most recent Form 990.
It is a public document. You are looking for what share of spending goes to programs rather than fundraising and administration.
Ask what your money funds, specifically.
A good organization can answer in one sentence. A vague answer is itself an answer.
Ask what you will receive and how often.
Letters, photographs, progress reports. Get the cadence in writing.
Ask what happens if you stop.
A well-run program has a plan for it. See the FAQ below.
Set up the gift and keep the receipt.
In the US, contributions to a 501(c)(3) are tax-deductible.
The question that tells you the most is the simplest one: what does my $25 buy this month? An organization that can answer it precisely is one that knows what it is doing.
How to check a charity before you give
You do not have to take anyone’s word for it. Four free sources:
IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search
Confirms 501(c)(3) status and that the organization is in good standing.
ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer
Publishes Form 990 filings, so you can see revenue and spending.
Candid
, formerly GuideStar.
Transparency ratings based on what the organization voluntarily discloses.
Charity Navigator
Ratings and financial analysis, though smaller organizations are sometimes unrated simply because of their size.
An organization that has not been rated is not necessarily a bad one. Ratings often require a revenue threshold. But an organization that will not show you its 990 is a different matter.
About Victoria Venezuela Foundation

We are a 501(c)(3) nonprofit based in Weston, Florida. Our EIN is 88-3282100. We hold a Candid Platinum Transparency seal, and in fiscal 2025, 95% of funds went directly to programs. Our annual reports are published on this site under Resources › Financials.
Frequently asked questions
How much does it cost to sponsor a child?
Large US programs ask $39 to $43 a month. At Victoria Venezuela Foundation, sponsorship starts at $25 a month.
What does my sponsorship actually pay for?

Your gifts fund three programs: a weekly nutrition program, medical attention twice a year, and an annual education program. Since 2022 they have served 77,300 meals, provided 1,012 medical visits for children and supported 99 children in school. The money funds the programs the child is enrolled in rather than going to the family as cash.
Is child sponsorship tax-deductible?
In the United States, yes, if the organization is a registered 501(c)(3). Victoria Venezuela Foundation is, under EIN 88-3282100. Keep your receipts.
What happens if I have to stop sponsoring?

Nothing happens to the child immediately. Well-run programs do not withdraw services when a sponsor leaves; gifts are pooled precisely so support stays steady while a new sponsor is found. Tell the organization rather than cancelling silently, so they can plan.
Can I write to the child I sponsor?
Yes. You can exchange letters with the child you sponsor and learn more about their life. You also see them grow through photos of our activities, and you can join our regular prayers for them.
Can I choose which child I sponsor?
Yes. Browse the children waiting for a sponsor and choose.
How is a small charity different from a large one?

Scale versus proximity. Large organizations have more infrastructure, more countries and audited reporting. Small ones can usually tell you more about the specific child and the specific place. Neither is automatically better.

A message from us

This 2025 was a beautiful testament witnessing love in action. Every smile, every moment of renewed hope, and every story of transformation reminded us why this mission matters so deeply. Our hearts are overflowing with gratitude for all that God allowed us to sow and pour into the lives of our 700+ children throughout 2025.

Week after week, our extraordinary volunteers showed up with unwavering dedication and excellence in all they do — preparing centers, serving meals, teaching, encouraging, and creating safe spaces filled with love. Their servant hearts fueled with love are the foundation of everything we do, and we are profoundly grateful for the countless hours they invested to ensure every child felt valued and supported. As scripture teaches us:
“You are the light of the world. Let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father who is in heaven.”
Matthew 5:14–16
This year also marked several major milestones that strengthened our support programs and impact:
Launched new nutrition support initiatives, extending kitchen infrastructure, tables and chairs helping increase the number of children receiving consistent meals
Expanded educational development programs, recognizing and celebrating the top 10% students and their academic performance
Golf Charity Tournament hosted 1st edition in Weston Hills, Florida joining over 40 corporate partners, providing the financial stability for long-term growth.
Enhanced technology integration and reporting systems, ensuring transparency, accountability, and readiness for scaling.

To our volunteers, strategic partners, and supporters: thank you for walking with us in faith and believing in this mission. Thank you for investing in these children and in Venezuela. Together, we are building futures filled with hope — making ways, one child and one family at a time.
With blessings,
Randy & Helen
Founders
Who we are

We are a non-profit foundation, 501(c)(3) Tax ID: 88-3282100, dedicated to paving the way for the most vulnerable children in Venezuela through its nutrition, medical care and education programs. Currently, two Support Centers have been established in Venezuela: Los Valles del Tuy, Miranda and Ciudad Bolívar, Bolívar.

We operate with a holistic and integrated approach with the Christian faith as the cornerstone of everything we do. We partner with local churches to provide guiding principles and values to the children we serve. Our cohesive support programs are designed to address the critical needs of children, helping to transform their future and enabling them to become a light to the world (Matthew 5:14).
Our Vision
Pave the way for vulnerable children throughout Venezuela by training them with biblical principles so that they can be light in the world.
Mission
Design support networks throughout Venezuela through food, medical care and education programs while teaching children to have a personal relationship with Jesus Christ
Our commitment

At the Victoria Venezuela Foundation, we are committed to making a significant impact in the lives of those most in need. We wholeheartedly believe that all children were made in the image of God. Children should be valued, respected and loved as God has shown us with his only son Jesus Christ.

The UN adopted the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, an opportunity for countries and their societies to embark on a new path to improve the lives of all people, leaving no one behind. Our team works on three (3) critical goals: zero hunger, good health and well-being and quality education to support the development of each child.
Governance policies and standards

Victoria Venezuela Foundation is dedicated to transparency across all its operations. By establishing clear policies and governance through the Board of Directors and the entire organization, we aim to successfully address effectiveness and risks.
Key policies and standards include:

Education Program:

excited to announce the launch of an impactful education program empowering vulnerable children in the Los Valles del Tuy, Miranda community. This initiative aims to provide essential school supplies, including backpacks, thermoses, pencils, and more, enabling these 24 children to reach their God-given potential.
FestiKids:

A Heartwarming Celebration drawing over 378 children in Ciudad Bolivar, Bolivar. This vibrant event dedicated to bringing love and compassion. The celebration was a resounding success, a day filled with joy, community spirit, and care. FestiKids offered a variety of activities designed to uplift and entertain, including fun games, arts and crafts, and engaging storytelling that shared the Word of God. The event not only provided children with essential food and clothing but also included complimentary haircuts, ensuring every child left feeling valued and refreshed.

We extend our heartfelt thanks to our donors, volunteers, and sponsors for their unwavering support. Your contributions have made a significant difference in the lives of vulnerable children, and we could not have achieved these milestones without you.

Victoria Venezuela Foundation remains dedicated to our mission: Design support networks throughout Venezuela with food and medical care programs while teaching children to have a personal relationship with Jesus Christ. We look forward to continuing our efforts with the same passion and commitment for the future of the Children in Venezuela.

Frequently asked questions
How many meals had the foundation served by the third quarter of 2024?
16,797 nutritious meals to vulnerable children, year to date.
How many children received medical attention?
The foundation’s volunteers and medical professionals attended to 350 children, year to date.
What was the new education program?
A program in the Los Valles del Tuy, Miranda community that provides school supplies, including backpacks, thermoses and pencils, to 24 children.
